independence.otherAuthorship: Reviewer authored ordinary and Staked refresh tests, which are outside this tool-defect review.

scope: Read-only independent adjudication of optional production --prices source binding in the shared Family historical runner. No source/test edits, RPC, cloud commands, native simulations, or acceptance reruns.

findings.cause: The --prices branch compares generation identifiers from independent price-runtime and Ready/execution lifecycle sessions as though they shared an identifier domain. Same canonical N/hash and exact readySha256 do not imply equal session generations.
findings.actualTrigger: pricing.generation=1 and Ready.cutoff.generation=25462190 at the same number and block hash. line138 rejects before inspecting the target row.

affectedAssertions.correction: Price runtime/pricing generations must agree internally; do not compare this value to Ready.cutoff.generation.
effective.source must fully equal the pricing source; its number/hash must equal the requested Ready/test chain state.
The required fresh target quote must be issued at effective.source, including the price session generation.
Report actual priceSource and executionSource separately; never relabel the donor generation.

findings.fact: The inspected fresh prices file contains zero quoted rows. The Staked route row status is missing-valuation with null amountIn/amountOut and no quotedAt.
findings.consequence: Correcting the session-generation false rejection must still reject this file as a usable natural effective-price donor. The correction does not itself establish production natural-valuation acceptance.

minimumCorrectBinding: Preserve schemaVersion and exact current readySha256 checks.

Derive the price-source triple from the runtime/pricing snapshot; require runtime, pricing and effective source number/hash/generation to agree internally. If graph source fields are validated, bind each to this price source too.
Require canonical number and hash of the price source to equal the requested tested state and Ready cutoff. A different N or hash must fail even if all price fields agree with one another.
Do not compare the price session generation to the Ready issuance/execution session generation, and do not rewrite either source.
Preserve exact target route/edge/token identity, complete=true, quoted row status, positive bigint input/output, positive finite raw mid, and fresh row.quotedAt equal to effective.source.
Keep execution source, generation fence, issued Family handles and Exact construction bound to the Ready cutoff. Saved prices are data donors and do not confer issuer authority.
Record actual priceSource and executionSource, including their distinct generations, in the report.
Do not globally require rawMidSource to equal current effective source: raw bootstrap/carry lineage can be older by design. The inspected file happens to match.
minimumBoundaryRegressionExpectations: Accept source binding for same number/hash and matching Ready bytes despite price generation1 versus Ready cutoff generation25462190, without normalizing either source.
Reject different canonical block number even when price-runtime components agree internally.
Reject different block hash even at the same number and with internally consistent pricing.
Reject internal runtime/pricing/effective generation mismatch and a target quote issued at a different price source.
Retain exact Ready hash/schema and quoted-row/positive-amount gates; actual missing-valuation rows remain unusable.

productionReferences.observation: Production checks effective source against its own pricing source triple.
Production publication binds effective source to current graph/session source triple.
prices.json serializes the runtime snapshot and binds its exact Ready input with readySha256.

existingManualEvidence.impact: No change to prior manual simulation evidence or production source is implied by this tool-only finding.

closureOwner: Parent owns the minimal helper fix, meaningful boundary regression, tooling_defect capture and final validation. This report confirms the defect but does not claim the proposed fix has been implemented or run.
